free_tier.stated: No free tier on the network itself: $0.023/GB/month, billed on encoded size, which is 'about 4.5x the original blob plus a fixed 64 MB of per-blob metadata'. Lighthouse resells Walrus with a 100 MB free plan.

egress.terms: No published free egress allowance; reads are served by Walrus storage nodes and aggregators. Cost is denominated in WAL + SUI gas per operation, so there is no 'free' path at all.

record.tooling: walrus CLI, TypeScript SDK, HTTP aggregator/publisher endpoints; Lighthouse wraps it as an IPFS-compatible layer.
record.chaining: None. Paid per GB-month with a 4.5x encoding tax. 500 GB of real data costs like 2.3 TB of billing.
record.limits_note: 4.5x encoded-size billing + 64 MB per-blob overhead; SUI gas per blob registration; epoch-based storage duration (must be extended).
record.reliability_note: The 64 MB per-blob metadata overhead is brutal for a data-science corpus of many small files: the docs' own worked example has 6 MB of 10 KiB files costing like 38.4 GB. Quilt batching mitigates but does not remove it.

evidence.proved: 'fixed, USD-denominated storage cost of $0.023/GB/month'; 'The encoded size is about 4.5x the original blob plus a fixed 64 MB of per-blob metadata'

record.notes: No free tier on the network itself: $0.023/GB/month, billed on encoded size, which is 'about 4.5x the original blob plus a fixed 64 MB of per-blob metadata'. Lighthouse resells Walrus with a 100 MB free plan.

card.summary: 5 GB free. Launched 2026-10-07 with 'Get started today with 5GB free'. No larger free tier is published.

free_tier.stated: 5 GB free. Launched 2026-10-07 with 'Get started today with 5GB free'. No larger free tier is published.

retention.stated: One week old at time of research. Storage is leased time, so 'free 5 GB' and 'kept forever' are not the same claim.

egress.terms: Reads via the Console API/MCP; the underlying Walrus network serves blobs from storage nodes. No egress meter published.

record.tooling: Genuinely good for an agent workflow: API keys plus an MCP server that plugs into Claude Code, Codex and Cursor; 'Agent Storage Loop' SDK for batched small writes with durability confirmation. Encrypted by default, per-file on-chain fingerprint.
record.chaining: The paid path is buying WAL and paying per epoch (storage is leased in time units, not bytes-forever). So cost scales with retention period × size, which is the opposite of an archive.
record.limits_note: Fails-quota at 5 GB by two orders of magnitude. Retention is epoch-based, so data expires unless renewed. A retention-clamped model at the protocol level.
record.reliability_note: One week old at time of research. Storage is leased time, so 'free 5 GB' and 'kept forever' are not the same claim.

evidence.proved: opened: 'Get started today with 5GB free'; published 07 Oct 2026; 'Every file gets a cryptographic fingerprint recorded onchain'; MCP integration with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor; 'encryption and renewals in one place' (note: renewals).

record.notes: 5 GB free. Launched 2026-10-07 with 'Get started today with 5GB free'. No larger free tier is published.
